hints: Focus on what it means to be a Group 1 metal, think about the outer electron configuration of Li, Na, K and the rest.
Remember how atomic size changes as you go down a group to a new period with more shells.
Compare a very reactive Period 8 alkali metal with a Period 7 noble gas, which type of atom holds its first electron much more tightly?
walkthrough:
**Check statement 1 - outer orbital**

All Group 1 elements have one outer electron in an s orbital. Li is $2s^1$, Na is $3s^1$, and so on.

So element 119 should be $8s^1$, meaning statement 1 is correct.

**Check statement 2 - atomic radius**

Atomic radius increases down a group because each new period adds a new principal shell and more shielding.

$$\text{radius: Li < Na < K < Rb < Cs < Fr < 119}$$

As the 7th member at the bottom of Group 1, element 119 will be largest, so statement 2 is correct.

**Check statement 3 - first ionisation energy**

First ionisation energy is very high for noble gases like element 118, and very low for Group 1 metals which lose one electron easily.

$$\text{Group 1 (low IE) < Group 18 (high IE)}$$

Element 119 will start a new period with a far, shielded $8s$ electron, so its first ionisation energy will be much smaller than that of 118, not greater. Statement 3 is incorrect.

**Combine the conclusions**

Only statements 1 and 2 are correct.

This matches the option for 1 and 2 only.

options.A: This option includes all three statements. Statements 1 and 2 are correct, but 3 is wrong because a Group 1 metal will have a far lower first ionisation energy than the noble gas element 118.
options.B: This option includes 1 and 2 only. Statement 1 is correct as a Group 1 element has an $ns^1$ outer configuration, so an s orbital. Statement 2 is correct as radius increases down the group, making Period 8 element 119 the largest.
options.C: This option includes 2 and 3 but omits 1. Statement 1 is actually correct and should be included, while statement 3 is incorrect, so this combination cannot be right.
options.D: This option includes 1 only. While statement 1 is correct, it wrongly leaves out statement 2, which is also correct because atomic radius increases down Group 1 to element 119.
